references.text: The goat is used as a sin offering, which is prescribed in the laws concerning sin offerings for leaders in Israel.
The burnt offering must be a male animal without defect, as here with the calf and the lamb that are to be 'temimim' (without defect).
A male goat without defect is used as a sin offering for the people.
A one-year-old lamb is used for the burnt offering, meeting the same requirements as in this text.
A one-year-old lamb without defect was required for the Passover sacrifice, showing the requirement for young, unblemished animals.
At the New Moon festival, young bulls, rams, and one-year-old lambs were to be offered as burnt offerings.
A male goat for a sin offering along with a burnt offering of a young bull, a ram, and one-year-old lambs.
Ezekiel describes future sacrifices involving unblemished bulls and rams, and a male goat for a sin offering.
The book of Hebrews explains how Christ fulfilled the sin offering and the burnt offering with his own blood, once for all.
